subject: Siloed GPU onboarding recap & SLO/SLA draft
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Park <lisa@medbyte.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Siloed GPU onboarding recap & SLO/SLA draft

Hi Lisa — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. I’ve kept this tight and added owners/timing.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Production inference variability under burst traffic; current on-prem infra is oversubscribed during end-of-day scoring windows.
- Data isolation requirements for model inputs/outputs (patient PII) plus customer-controlled KMS for keys.
- Strict SLA needs for your core inference API (sensitive workflows) with short tail latency targets.

Stated goals (today):
- Move to an isolated, Redwood-hosted Dedicated pool with tenant-level isolation (no cross-tenant inference).
- Baseline capacity: 10 reserved GPUs for immediate steady-state with the ability to burst to 20 for scheduled scoring windows.
- Encryption-in-transit and at-rest with integration to your KMS; SOC2 evidence for controls.
- Target SLOs: availability 99.95% for reserved pool, p50 latency goal <80ms, p99 <400ms for typical text-generation workloads (we can tighten after canary).

Technical proposal we discussed:
- Reserved pool: 10x A100-class GPUs (customer-isolated pool). Burst policy to allow auto-burst to a backed capacity of up to 20 GPUs for scheduled jobs (30m max burst per window, configurable).
- Isolation: dedicated tenant + VPC peering or PrivateLink; optional on-prem connector for hybrid KV-cache sync.
- Rollout: 2-week canary (10% traffic), scale to 50% after 48h if telemetry stable, full cutover in 10 business days.
- Observability: per-route token-level cost/latency dashboard + alerting to MedByte paging channel.

Next steps (owners / ETA):
1) Share single-page SLO/SLA draft for review — Stephanie (EOD 11/23) — attached.
2) Security/compliance packet request: SOC2 excerpt + network isolation checklist — Lisa to confirm what you need; we’ll prep our side.
3) Technical kickoff — 30–45m with infra + SRE to agree network and KMS integration — proposed 11/25; Karthik to lead.
4) Cost estimate for baseline+burst — Markus to send a 12-month TCO (incl. reserved discounts) — target 11/24.

Questions I have for you (short):
- Confirm the burst window cadence and any blackout windows (overnight scoring windows you already mentioned would be helpful).
- Any hard p99 latency requirement that must be met to keep the contract?

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf (SLO targets + escalation paths), Network_Isolation_Checklist.xlsx (initial checklist), Onboarding-MOP-draft.txt (ops playbook).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the technical kickoff once you confirm 11/25 works.

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0122

From: Lisa Park <lisa@medbyte.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom@medbyte.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T17:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Siloed GPU onboarding recap & SLO/SLA draft

Thanks, Stephanie — good write-up and appreciated. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Burst windows: we have two predictable scoring windows each day (03:30–04:15 PT and 21:00–21:45 PT). We’d like burst to be available for both windows for at least 45 minutes.
2) Latency: for our regulatory workflows the hard requirement is p99 < 300ms. If that’s not achievable with the baseline configuration, we’ll need a guaranteed escalation path in the SLA with remediation credits.
3) Security: SOC2 excerpt is a must; also need evidence of tenant isolation (network diagrams) and confirmation that Redwood will not retain raw inputs longer than 30 days by default.

We’ll review the SLA draft you attached and share headcount availability for the kickoff. Tom (cc’d) will handle the network checklist items.

Also: can you include an estimate for an optional on-prem connector (hybrid mode) — not required day 1 but we want pricing and rough timeline.

I’ll aim to have our internal list of blackout windows and SOC2 request items back to you by end of day Thursday (11/25).

Best,
Lisa Park
CTO, MedByte AI
lisa@medbyte.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T20:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Siloed GPU onboarding recap & SLO/SLA draft (internal)

Looping in a quick technical read on Lisa’s asks so we can prepare for the kickoff: 

Notes:
- The p99 <300ms requirement is aggressive for certain long-context generation workloads; we should propose a two-tier SLA: critical-regulatory routes (pin to higher priority workers / smaller batch sizes / more conservative quantization) with tighter p99, and standard routes with the baseline p99.<n>- For the reserved pool sizing: 10x A100 should cover steady-state inference for the metrics Lisa described, but the burst to 20 (45m windows) will increase token-cost. Need Markus to produce the cost delta for burst capacity and a recommended autoscaling policy (min 10, max 20, graceful ramp).
- KMS: we can support customer-managed keys via the KMS integration; ops will require a brief key handoff playbook.

Action items for call:
- I’ll prepare a short ops diagram showing VPC peering + PrivateLink options (deliverable 11/24).
- Recommend we include a small canary with synthetic traffic that exercises the regulatory route at ~120% baseline to validate p99.

Karthik
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Park <lisa@medbyte.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Tom Nguyen <tom@medbyte.ai>
Date: 2026-11-23T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Final: SLO/SLA draft & next calendar steps

Hi Lisa — attaching the SLA draft with a short addendum that captures the two-tier SLA approach Karthik recommended (we’ll tighten after canary). I’ve also added a section for remediation credits tied specifically to the regulatory routes (per your ask).

Attachments in this message: Redwood_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf, Network_Isolation_Checklist.xlsx, Onboarding-MOP-draft.txt, SOC2-Excerpt-MedByte-requested.pdf (redacted excerpt).

Proposed immediate timeline:
- 11/24: Price/TCO from Markus + ops diagram from Karthik
- 11/25: Technical kickoff (30m) — proposed slots 9:00am or 2:00pm PT. Please reply with preferred slot; Tom, Karthik & I will be on the call.
- 11/27–12/08: Canary + validation window (two weeks), followed by scaling to full production if telemetry meets SLOs.

If that works, I’ll create a DocuSign-ready SLA after the kickoff and route for signature.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

— Stephanie
